newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian LNG says awaits Enel new proposals on gas.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian LNG says awaits Enel new proposals on gas.

text.p: Nigerian liquefied natural gas (NLNG) company is awaiting specific proposals from Italian state utility Enel on how it will take the full volume of LNG it originally signed to buy from Nigeria, a company statement said on Friday.

Oil minister Dan Etete, who said he went to Italy for talks on the NLNG-Enel face-off, told reporters on Thursday in Lagos that Enel had reversed its earlier decision to cancel a contract signed with NLNG to purchase its gas.

"We are awaiting specific proposals from ENEL regarding the ways in which they would receive and pay for the LNG from Nigeria," the statement said, adding: "NLNG cannot pre-judge the outcome of such discussions."

Enel last December cancelled a long-term contract to buy the Nigerian LNG, citing its abandonment of a project to construct a gas plant at Montalto di Castro, north of Rome, for economic, technical and environmental reasons.
Etete said: "Enel is now taking the entire volume of gas it signed with Nigerian LNG. All issues have been resolved and the Italian government is fully in support of the Nigerian LNG project."

But Steve Ollerearnshaw, NLNG's managing director, told Reuters on Friday: "We are awaiting detailed information on how Enel had reversed cancellation of the contract. We cannot say the problem has been resolved when we have not been briefed by Enel."

Ollerearnshaw said arbitration proceedings which were immediately launched in Switzerland after Enel cancelled the contract were still on. NLNG said at the time they were certain to win and recover billions of dollars from Enel.
The Italian firm signed the contract in November and was to receive the first cargo of LNG in the third quarter of 1999.

Nigeria's $4 billion LNG project, now in full swing in the southeastern oil-producing area of Bonny, is to produce 7.2 billion cubic metres of LNG per year from a plant projected to start production in 1999.
Under the November accord, Enel was to take 3.5 billion cubic metres of the output annually.
Partners in the project are the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation, Shell Gas BV, Elf Aquitaine ELF.PA and Italy's Agip SpA.
Long-term supply contracts have been signed with Enargas of Spain, Gaz de France and Botas of Turkey.
